newsitem.title: CROATIA: Klein says poll in E.Slavonia may be extended.
newsitem.headline: Klein says poll in E.Slavonia may be extended.

text.p: U.N. administrator Jacques Klein allowed on Sunday for a possibility that elections in the Serb Eastern Slavonia region may be extended into Monday to rectify many technical problems that have plagued the start of the landmark Croatian municipal poll.

"That is an option. We will look into that this afternoon. I will not disenfranchise anyone," Klein told reporters, responding to a question whether the polls might be extended into Monday after numerous delays in polling stations across the area, due to technical problems.

The polls were supposed to have opened at 7 a.m., but by 9.30 a.m. only around 100 out of 171 voting stations in Eastern Slavonia were operating, the spokesman for the U.N. Administration, Philip Arnold told reporters.
Reuters reporters in the village of Pacetin saw local Serbs crowding in front of a school from early morning, only to be told to come later as voting materials had not arrived on time.
"There were some logistical problems. We had mismatched ballot packages, some of which were delivered to wrong places," Arnold earlier told Reuters on the telephone from his Vukovar headquarters.
Arnold said confusion was compounded by late registering of Serbs for Croatian documents which in turn led to last-minute revisions of voting lists.

Eastern Slavonia Serbs are taking part for the first time since 1990 in Croatian municipal and Upper House poll, ahead of the region's reintegration with the rest of the country scheduled for mid-July.
